children: Canadian telco Quebecor says a tie-up between BCE's Bell Canada and Telus would hurt consumers, saying Bell has generated a high number of customer complaints. The statement follows a Globe and Mail report that BCE has opened preliminary talks with Telus. Quebecor says that Bell "ranks among the telecommunications providers generating the highest number of complaints filed with the Commission for Complaints for Telecom-television Services," an independent consumer agency. It says in the press release that Bell recently imposed rate increases on its mobile customers, while continuing to charge unwanted fees--despite a regulatory ban on such charges. Quebecor contrasts that record with its Freedom Mobile unit, saying its own C$31.31 billion bid for Telus would better protect competition and pricing. A BCE spokesperson declined to comment. (adriano.marchese@wsj.com)
